correctness.rationale: For positive fixed pulse amounts, constant competition K, death rate and horizon, exact piecewise integration gives F_q(y). Its derivative has sign opposite the strictly increasing quadratic g_q(y), so an endpoint maximizer or a unique interior global maximizer exists and the cutoff is exact, including equality. The root equation yields strict horizon monotonicity and derivative bounds; a direct sign test at sqrt(q) yields the sharp midpoint crossing and the strict order of two horizons. The exact asymptotic follows by expansion of the positive root. An extracted standalone Python checker completed 187,417 supplementary assertions, including quadrature independent of the closed integral; sampled checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The model isolates the biologically interpretable question of how the timing of a second fixed sterile-male batch alters aggregate competition against fertile males. It provides an exact simultaneous-vs-staggered boundary and a distinct, nonobvious midpoint reversal that requires an unequal dose threshold; it also identifies where a universal half-horizon heuristic fails. The all-parameter formula, strict global uniqueness, comparative statics and limits create a checkable baseline for coupled ecological-control models, while limitations explicitly prohibit extrapolation to eradication or clinical impact.
